208 of 208 pain points · All merchant types
These are synthesized pain hypotheses, not interview quotes. Source links establish related workflows; frequency and severity still need merchant validation. Coverage scores are analyst estimates, not measured percentages solved. Open a bucket, then a subtree, then a pain point.
01

Establish and control the business

Become eligible to trade and keep systems, people and automation under control.

20 pains

Before opening, Priya needs payment activation. Later, a former contractor still has account access and a connector silently stops syncing.

Classification boundary

Owns entity/processor access, technology reliability, permissions, privacy and business continuity. Transaction fraud belongs in 07; tax recordkeeping in 08; staff cost/payment in 10.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay covers onboarding, payment integration and agent controls. RAY helps navigate payment operations. General incorporation, enterprise IT and whole-business continuity remain broader than these products.

Research hypothesis · All
Underlying need

Outcome to measure
Time to first live payment; launch days lost.

Payment integration / financial-system events

Observable by the relevant fintech product

↳ 1C. Roles and accountable delegation4 pains

Latent need hypothesis
I want to delegate routine work without handing over control of all my money and customer data.

01.3.1Staff share the owner login because roles are inconvenientRP 3/5
Research hypothesis · Retail, B2B, Service
Underlying need
Give each person only the permissions required for their work.
Observable signals
Shared logins; broad roles; owner-only bottlenecks.
Outcome to measure
Unauthorized changes; approval waiting time.
R03 · Razorpay, U07 · Square
Direct fintech roleIntegration / execution gap

Where finance touches this pain

Account permissions / payment approvals

Observable by the relevant fintech product
Users, roles, approval queues and recorded financial actions.
Requires merchant-connected data
Employment status, agency contracts, delegated limits and escalation contacts.
What this could enable — proposed, not a product claim
Recommend least-privilege access and route time-sensitive approvals. Specific need: Give each person only the permissions required for their work.
Boundary
Revoking one account does not revoke every external credential.

02

Choose the offer and prepare supply

Have the right product, service capacity and economics ready before selling.

20 pains

Priya runs out of popular refills while gift sets sit unsold. A wholesale order looks attractive until she includes packing, shipping and credit terms.

Classification boundary

Owns assortment, base pricing, supplier readiness, inventory and capacity planning. Executing an accepted order belongs in 06; paying suppliers in 10.

Razorpay coverage

RazorpayX AP Automation covers supplier onboarding, purchase orders, invoice intake and matching. These are meaningful procurement capabilities. SKU demand, physical stock, product costing and capacity planning still require merchant operational systems.

Acquire qualified new demand

Help suitable new customers discover and trust the business at an affordable cost.

20 pains

Priya buys ads but sees visits without profitable first orders. She cannot tell whether a creator campaign brought customers or only views.

Classification boundary

Owns discovery through qualified interest from prospective customers. Checkout friction belongs in 04; campaigns to previous buyers in 09.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay Engage supports acquisition and transaction-led promotions; Magic Checkout affects later conversion. GoKwik and commerce tools span more channels. No blanket claim that Razorpay lacks marketing or AI campaigns.

04

Convert intent into an agreed order

Help an interested customer confidently choose and commit to an order, quote or booking.

20 pains

A customer likes Priya’s gift set but leaves after seeing shipping charges. Another cannot complete checkout comfortably on a phone.

Classification boundary

Owns choice, cart, price disclosure and order commitment. Processing the payment instruction belongs in 05; inventory planning in 02. An abandoned checkout with no attempted payment belongs here.

Razorpay coverage

Magic Checkout, offers/affordability and Agent Studio cart recovery directly overlap this bucket. Shopify, GoKwik and Gorgias supply comparable or adjacent workflows.

05

Collect the agreed customer payment

Turn an authorized amount due into one verified successful collection.

20 pains

Priya sees failed UPI payments, an unpaid wholesale invoice and a subscription renewal that did not debit. Each requires a different recovery action.

Classification boundary

Owns payment authorization, failures, recurring debits and overdue invoices. Funds already collected but not received/matched belong in 08. Voluntary relationship churn belongs in 09.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay payments, Optimizer, UPI AutoPay, recovery agents, payment links and Smart Collect cover substantial parts. Do not frame generic retries or invoice reminders as missing capabilities.

06

Deliver the promised value

Complete each accepted order or service reliably, at a sustainable cost.

20 pains

Priya has paid orders waiting to be packed, a courier pickup that did not happen and two customers marked unreachable.

Classification boundary

Owns order execution, dispatch, delivery, service delivery and failed-delivery/RTO prevention. Post-delivery returns or compensation belong in 07; stock planning in 02; carrier COD remittance in 08.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay Magic Checkout and Agent Studio address COD confirmation, RTO risk and feedback. They are not evidenced as full warehouse, dispatch or service-delivery systems. Shiprocket, Zoho and Square cover adjacent execution.

07

Resolve exceptions and protect value

Handle returns, refunds, disputes and fraud fairly while limiting avoidable loss.

20 pains

A delivered item arrives damaged, a customer asks for an exchange, and a bank dispute arrives with a deadline. Priya needs distinct policies and evidence for each.

Classification boundary

Owns contested/reversed transactions and loss protection, including transaction-fraud decisions before payment. Failed payment execution is 05; failed delivery prevention is 06; future relationship retention is 09.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay supports refunds, wallet refunds and Agent Studio dispute response. Magic Checkout provides risk controls. Public evidence here does not establish a complete AI product-exchange optimizer; Return Prime and Loop show deeper returns workflows.

08

Receive, reconcile and account for money

Know where collected money is, match it to business records and produce trustworthy accounts.

20 pains

Priya’s sales report, courier COD statement and bank balance all differ. Her accountant needs to separate normal timing from missing funds or incorrect deductions.

Classification boundary

Owns settlement, remittance, matching, fee audit and financial/tax records. Unpaid customer obligations are 05; cash allocation and financing decisions are 10.

Razorpay coverage

Razorpay settlements, reports, Smart Collect and RAY cover substantial payment visibility and matching. Whole-ledger reconciliation, tax close and revenue recognition require additional systems and context.

09

Retain and grow existing relationships

Earn another useful, profitable purchase and keep customers who still value the offer.

20 pains

Priya knows many buyers never return but does not know whether to wait, remind, educate, recommend another product or offer a benefit.

Classification boundary

Owns post-purchase relationship, voluntary churn, loyalty, replenishment and expansion. Failed debits are 05; a live refund/dispute is 07; acquisition of genuinely new buyers is 03.

Razorpay coverage

Engage and BillMe already offer customer data, segmentation, loyalty and automated campaigns. AutoPay has cancellation win-back. Individual next-purchase prediction and causal profit measurement remain unverified in reviewed Razorpay public materials.

10

Fund and sustain business operations

Have enough affordable cash, people and operating discipline to keep promises and grow.

28 pains

Priya can show accounting profit but must pay salaries and a supplier before receivables and COD cash arrive. Growth creates a funding gap.

Classification boundary

Owns liquidity planning, financing, supplier/staff payments, recurring spend and business resource allocation. Supply selection is 02; customer collections 05; accounting facts 08; permissions and continuity controls 01. Insurance risk transfer and treasury policy also live here; transaction disputes remain in 07.

Razorpay coverage

RazorpayX covers AP, payouts, payroll, corporate cards and connected banking. Credit availability is account-specific; historical Capital material is separated from current card products. Insurance and treasury investing were not verified as dedicated merchant workflows.

Prioritization · working hypotheses

Growth priorities

64 pain points ranked within this outcome.

Create additional demand, improve conversion before a specific failure, or increase useful repeat purchases and customer value. Includes measurement and data prerequisites; these are explicitly labelled.

Choose what to validate next. Scores express analyst judgment, not measured market size or guaranteed returns. All 208 pains have one primary home across these three tabs. Similar ranks are a discussion prompt: differences of 5 points or less are not decision-grade evidence.

How to read the solution directions and related-pain families

Two independent choices: ML/deep learning describe the model; agentic/fixed workflow describes how work is coordinated. Deep learning is a subset of ML. A pretrained LLM is deep learning, while a forecast may use simpler statistical or tree models. A deterministic workflow can act automatically without being an AI agent.

Four directional approaches: Rules/statistics/workflow for known calculations and transitions; predictive ML plus a fixed workflow for forecasts or rankings; a grounded LLM copilot for interpretation/drafting; a hybrid agent plus rules when the next tool or action depends on intermediate evidence. “Candidate agent” is a hypothesis to test against a fixed workflow.

Build on / extend / adjacent: Build on means configure or reuse an existing product capability; extend adds a specific missing decision or exception to its direction; adjacent needs a new workflow. Product descriptions do not prove a public callable agent API, developer access or general availability. Razorpay’s proprietary model choices are not being inferred from these proposed architectures.

Training and cold start: Rules need verified records; pretrained LLMs need approved knowledge and evaluation examples; supervised models need labelled outcomes; time-to-event models need censored cases; uplift needs credible treatment assignment. Start with a simple baseline when data is sparse. There is no universal minimum row count: determine sufficiency using learning curves, temporal validation and experimental power. No cross-merchant training permission is assumed.

Families: Related pains are grouped into pairs or triples where one user job, data flow or reusable control connects them. Original IDs and ranks stay intact; a family is not a selected solution or summed business case. Mixed-outcome families share components while keeping growth, collection, cost and cash measures separate. Unrelated pains remain standalone.

Evidence: Razorpay links establish advertised capability, and model references explain available methods. The proposed model, flow, controls and learning loop are our design hypotheses. Scores have not been recalibrated in this pass; the solution assessment is more specific than the earlier broad AI-advantage rating.

Scoring framework, weights & classification boundaries

Weighted opportunity score = Σ(weight × rating ÷ 5) ÷ Σ(weights) × 100. Every factor is 0–5, with higher better. Default weights sum to 100; edits are normalized automatically. Scores are comparable within this tab under the same weights, not across tabs with different objectives.

Why these weights: Growth gives more weight to contextual AI advantage and reach; recovery gives more to case frequency and executable data/action paths; other opportunities balance operating impact, frequency and feasibility. Room to improve is intentionally limited to 10–15% so an unsupported competitive gap cannot dominate.

FactorWhat we judgeAnchors; intermediate scores interpolate
Value at stakePotential net benefit per affected merchant, conditional on the problem existing. Growth: incremental fulfilled contribution; recovery: valid net collections or retained sales; other: avoided cost, cash delay or control harm.0: no outcome path · 1: small inconvenience · 3: material recurring loss/effort · 5: business-critical value at risk
FrequencyHow often an affected merchant encounters the decision. Kept separate from severity; an infrequent loss may still have high value.0: no recurring case · 1: exceptional/annual · 3: monthly or episodic clusters · 5: daily or across many transactions
ReachRelative breadth across the seven merchant lenses in this atlas. This is a qualitative proxy, not TAM, merchant counts or measured prevalence.0: no identifiable audience · 1: narrow edge case · 3: meaningful segment · 5: several broad merchant types
Room to improveResidual workflow gap after considering existing Razorpay products and the proposed enhancement. Scored independently; not simply 5 minus the coverage score.0: no credible extra job · 1: mainly adoption/configuration · 3: integration or exception gap · 5: no direct workflow identified and a concrete unmet job
Data & actionAbility to access authorised reliable signals and complete a controllable, reviewable intervention in a first pilot. Includes integration effort, action risk and dependencies.0: inaccessible or prohibited · 1: missing signal/action route · 3: plausible connector plus human approval · 5: reliable authorised data and bounded action already available
AI advantageBenefit of prediction, interpretation or contextual coordination over a simple rule, existing product or manual baseline. AI includes statistical ML; an LLM is not required for every step.0: unnecessary · 1: rules/arithmetic sufficient · 3: mixed context with plausible AI benefit · 5: essential contextual reasoning with a credible evaluable advantage
MeasurabilityAbility to attribute and verify the outcome, including costs, reversals and a comparison baseline.0: no observable result · 1: indirect/long-lag · 3: observable with attribution limits · 5: identifiable obligations/orders and a feasible controlled comparison

Evidence confidence: All ranks are provisional. Product documentation supports capability presence, not pain prevalence, money at stake or willingness to pay. Relative value/frequency/reach are assumptions. Razorpay coverage remains a separate 0–5 evidence assessment; its inverse is not used as the priority score. A low-coverage workflow may be outside fintech’s practical control.

Eligibility for an AI concept: AI advantage 0–2 → rules or existing tools first. AI ≥3 but data/action ≤2 → validate access first. AI ≥3 and data/action ≥3 → explore an AI enhancement. These labels do not alter the numerical ranking or guarantee feasibility. Do not use an LLM for payment arithmetic, authorisation or idempotency.

One outcome per pain: Abandoned carts, failed renewals, delivery exceptions, exchanges and cancellation saves are recovery. Routine repeat purchases, upsells, initial conversion and false-decline improvement are growth. COD remittance, settlement release, excess-fee refunds, insurance claims, avoided fraud cost, cashflow and governance are other. B2B collection is recovery of an existing obligation, usually a cash outcome rather than new recognised revenue. A measurement or identity prerequisite stays with the commercial outcome it enables and is labelled as an enabler.

Merchant scope: Default ranks span the seven merchant lenses in this atlas. Filter to a segment before selecting a project. “All” means broadly applicable; it does not prove every merchant experiences the pain. Reach is a qualitative breadth proxy, not an estimate of Indian market size. Multi-SKU inventory, B2B and subscription pain points need their own narrower segment validation.

Double-counting: Related pains may form one concept. For example 09.2.1 + 09.3.2 + 09.5.3, 05.4.2 + 05.4.3, and 03.2.4 + 03.4.1 share upside. Never sum their potential benefits. Scores exclude any invented rupee/TAM figures. To size a pilot: eligible cases × current avoidable loss × incremental improvement, less intervention, incentive and reversal costs; estimate each input from real merchant data.

Refresh on 13 October 2026: Existing Engage/BillMe, Agent Studio, AutoPay and receivables capabilities were considered. Current product/account access remains unverified. The later Agent Studio terms clarify that pause stops new runs while in-progress runs may finish, and authorised sub-processors may process data. See P01. No cross-merchant model training or blanket data access is assumed.

Factor ratings: 0–5 · RP = current Razorpay coverage · priority = weighted score /100. Click any heading to sort. Open a row for the residual gap, data, AI rationale, outcome and evidence.

Start with a simple baseline when data is sparse. There is no universal minimum row count: determine sufficiency using learning curves, temporal validation and experimental power. No cross-merchant training permission is assumed.

Families: Related pains are grouped into pairs or triples where one user job, data flow or reusable control connects them. Original IDs and ranks stay intact; a family is not a selected solution or summed business case. Mixed-outcome families share components while keeping growth, collection, cost and cash measures separate. Unrelated pains remain standalone.

Evidence: Razorpay links establish advertised capability, and model references explain available methods. The proposed model, flow, controls and learning loop are our design hypotheses. Scores have not been recalibrated in this pass; the solution assessment is more specific than the earlier broad AI-advantage rating.

Scoring framework, weights & classification boundaries

Weighted opportunity score = Σ(weight × rating ÷ 5) ÷ Σ(weights) × 100. Every factor is 0–5, with higher better. Default weights sum to 100; edits are normalized automatically. Scores are comparable within this tab under the same weights, not across tabs with different objectives.

Why these weights: Growth gives more weight to contextual AI advantage and reach; recovery gives more to case frequency and executable data/action paths; other opportunities balance operating impact, frequency and feasibility. Room to improve is intentionally limited to 10–15% so an unsupported competitive gap cannot dominate.

FactorWhat we judgeAnchors; intermediate scores interpolate
Value at stakePotential net benefit per affected merchant, conditional on the problem existing. Growth: incremental fulfilled contribution; recovery: valid net collections or retained sales; other: avoided cost, cash delay or control harm.0: no outcome path · 1: small inconvenience · 3: material recurring loss/effort · 5: business-critical value at risk
FrequencyHow often an affected merchant encounters the decision. Kept separate from severity; an infrequent loss may still have high value.0: no recurring case · 1: exceptional/annual · 3: monthly or episodic clusters · 5: daily or across many transactions
ReachRelative breadth across the seven merchant lenses in this atlas. This is a qualitative proxy, not TAM, merchant counts or measured prevalence.0: no identifiable audience · 1: narrow edge case · 3: meaningful segment · 5: several broad merchant types
Room to improveResidual workflow gap after considering existing Razorpay products and the proposed enhancement. Scored independently; not simply 5 minus the coverage score.0: no credible extra job · 1: mainly adoption/configuration · 3: integration or exception gap · 5: no direct workflow identified and a concrete unmet job
Data & actionAbility to access authorised reliable signals and complete a controllable, reviewable intervention in a first pilot. Includes integration effort, action risk and dependencies.0: inaccessible or prohibited · 1: missing signal/action route · 3: plausible connector plus human approval · 5: reliable authorised data and bounded action already available
AI advantageBenefit of prediction, interpretation or contextual coordination over a simple rule, existing product or manual baseline. AI includes statistical ML; an LLM is not required for every step.0: unnecessary · 1: rules/arithmetic sufficient · 3: mixed context with plausible AI benefit · 5: essential contextual reasoning with a credible evaluable advantage
MeasurabilityAbility to attribute and verify the outcome, including costs, reversals and a comparison baseline.0: no observable result · 1: indirect/long-lag · 3: observable with attribution limits · 5: identifiable obligations/orders and a feasible controlled comparison

Evidence confidence: All ranks are provisional. Product documentation supports capability presence, not pain prevalence, money at stake or willingness to pay. Relative value/frequency/reach are assumptions. Razorpay coverage remains a separate 0–5 evidence assessment; its inverse is not used as the priority score. A low-coverage workflow may be outside fintech’s practical control.

Eligibility for an AI concept: AI advantage 0–2 → rules or existing tools first. AI ≥3 but data/action ≤2 → validate access first. AI ≥3 and data/action ≥3 → explore an AI enhancement. These labels do not alter the numerical ranking or guarantee feasibility. Do not use an LLM for payment arithmetic, authorisation or idempotency.

One outcome per pain: Abandoned carts, failed renewals, delivery exceptions, exchanges and cancellation saves are recovery. Routine repeat purchases, upsells, initial conversion and false-decline improvement are growth. COD remittance, settlement release, excess-fee refunds, insurance claims, avoided fraud cost, cashflow and governance are other. B2B collection is recovery of an existing obligation, usually a cash outcome rather than new recognised revenue. A measurement or identity prerequisite stays with the commercial outcome it enables and is labelled as an enabler.

Merchant scope: Default ranks span the seven merchant lenses in this atlas. Filter to a segment before selecting a project. “All” means broadly applicable; it does not prove every merchant experiences the pain. Reach is a qualitative breadth proxy, not an estimate of Indian market size. Multi-SKU inventory, B2B and subscription pain points need their own narrower segment validation.

Double-counting: Related pains may form one concept. For example 09.2.1 + 09.3.2 + 09.5.3, 05.4.2 + 05.4.3, and 03.2.4 + 03.4.1 share upside. Never sum their potential benefits. Scores exclude any invented rupee/TAM figures. To size a pilot: eligible cases × current avoidable loss × incremental improvement, less intervention, incentive and reversal costs; estimate each input from real merchant data.

How to read the solution directions and related-pain families

Two independent choices: ML/deep learning describe the model; agentic/fixed workflow describes how work is coordinated. Deep learning is a subset of ML. A pretrained LLM is deep learning, while a forecast may use simpler statistical or tree models. A deterministic workflow can act automatically without being an AI agent.

Four directional approaches: Rules/statistics/workflow for known calculations and transitions; predictive ML plus a fixed workflow for forecasts or rankings; a grounded LLM copilot for interpretation/drafting; a hybrid agent plus rules when the next tool or action depends on intermediate evidence. “Candidate agent” is a hypothesis to test against a fixed workflow.

Build on / extend / adjacent: Build on means configure or reuse an existing product capability; extend adds a specific missing decision or exception to its direction; adjacent needs a new workflow. Product descriptions do not prove a public callable agent API, developer access or general availability. Razorpay’s proprietary model choices are not being inferred from these proposed architectures.

Training and cold start: Rules need verified records; pretrained LLMs need approved knowledge and evaluation examples; supervised models need labelled outcomes; time-to-event models need censored cases; uplift needs credible treatment assignment. No cross-merchant training permission is assumed.

Rank

Fictional composite, not an interview subject

Priya, founder of Nila Home

Business
An independent Bengaluru home-care and fragrance brand selling cleaning refills, candles and gift sets.

Scale
Illustrative operating assumptions: 6 employees, 1 physical shop, 1 small stockroom, around 1,200 monthly orders, and about 45 product variants. These are invented to make scenarios concrete, not market benchmarks.

Channels
Shop counter, own online store, WhatsApp inquiries, occasional marketplace sales and a small wholesale account base.

Payments
UPI, cards, selected COD orders and bank transfers against wholesale invoices. A refill subscription is a possible next stage, not an assumption that every customer subscribes.

Team
Priya makes commercial decisions; a store lead handles retail; an operations lead handles stock and shipping; a part-time accountant closes the books. Roles overlap when someone is absent.

Goals
Pay the team and suppliers on time; deliver reliably; know real contribution; earn repeat business; grow without losing control.

Tensions
Sales versus usable cash; recovery versus customer trust; automation versus control; growth versus working capital; more data versus time to decide.

A day in the business

08:30Check usable cash and supplier billsBuckets 08,10
09:30Receive stock and investigate mismatched countsBuckets 02
10:30Review new-customer inquiries and campaignsBuckets 03
12:00Handle a checkout problem and verify a pending paymentBuckets 04,05
14:00Pack orders and resolve a missed pickupBuckets 06
16:00Review a return and a dispute deadlineBuckets 07
17:30Contact a wholesale customer about an overdue invoiceBuckets 05
18:00Consider a repeat-purchase campaign and its economicsBuckets 09
19:00Reconcile deposits, review approvals and switch off an unsafe workflowBuckets 08,01

Other merchant lives

Solo

Individual seller / freelancer

Few transactions, minimal staff, phone-first work. Simplicity, cash confirmation and invoice follow-up matter; sophisticated experiments may be infeasible.

Retail

Physical or omnichannel retailer

Queues, cash/UPI confirmation, inventory across locations, returns and repeat visits.

Online

D2C / ecommerce company

Acquisition, checkout, payment failures, shipping, COD, returns and cross-channel attribution.

B2B

Wholesaler / professional services business

Quotes, trade credit, milestones, deductions, large receivables and supplier finance.

Subscription

Recurring goods or digital service

Mandates, failed renewals, plan changes, entitlement, voluntary cancellation and earned-revenue timing.

Service

Salon, clinic-like appointment business, tutor or studio

Bookable capacity, staff calendars, no-shows, deposits, service completion and repeat appointments. Sector-specific clinical/legal obligations are outside this map.

Food

Cafe / food merchant

Perishability, time-sensitive production, staffing, delivery and daily cash. Food-specific licensing and safety requirements require a dedicated extension.

Fintech across the whole business

Read the role, then the score.

All 200 original pains are retained. Eight additions make insurance and treasury explicit. Every pain has a fintech data map, a Razorpay assessment and two comparison providers.

0 does not prove absence. 5 requires more than a feature page.

Analyst-estimated coverage of the specific merchant job, not measured percent solved, product quality, market share or investment intensity.

Score within the specified merchant segment. Square US, Mondu UK/EU and Mercury US are design comparisons, not recommendations or proof of availability to Priya in India. No overall vendor average is presented because the scale is ordinal and the needs differ.

  1. No direct support identified in reviewed evidence; absence is unverified, not proof the company has never built it.
  2. Enabling input or adjacent feature; the merchant still assembles most of the solution.
  3. Partial coverage: a useful part of the job is addressed, with material gaps or limited rollout.
  4. Substantial workflow coverage; important integrations, exceptions or manual decisions remain.
  5. Strong documented coverage for the specified segment and configured workflow; real-world pain may remain.
  6. Mostly addressed for a narrowly defined eligible job, supported by implementation and outcome evidence. No 5 is assigned in this desk review.

Fintech touchpoints and data requirements

Native means observable by the appropriate fintech product if it is actually used—not automatically held by Razorpay. Connected data needs a permitted purpose, merchant authorization, relevant customer consent and appropriate access controls. Cross-merchant training or reuse is not assumed.

Direct: a financial product can execute a material part of the job. Data-enabled: useful intervention needs financial and operating data joined. Adjacent: finance measures or funds the consequence; an operating tool does the main work.

01 · Establish and control the business

1A. Eligibility and activation · Direct

Touchpoint: Merchant onboarding / KYB / account verification

Product-native: Submitted business identity, verification status and bank details.

Connect: Entity documents, ownership changes, category and country requirements.

Possible help: Explain rejection reasons and prepare a verifiable activation checklist.

Boundary: The fintech cannot bypass underwriting, sanctions or bank approval.

Stripe — Atlas / account setup · Core fintech
Company setup and account administration workflows. Incorporation is not payment approval; local requirements still apply.
U01 · F12

Setu — Account Aggregator gateway · Fintech infrastructure
Consent and financial-data fetch infrastructure. Requires eligible participants and permitted purpose; not unrestricted data access.
F21

1B. Systems and integration · Direct

Touchpoint: Payment integration / financial-system events

Product-native: Payment requests, API errors, event IDs, timestamps and delivery attempts.

Connect: Store order IDs, inventory/ERP sync status and deployment history.

Possible help: Trace failures, deduplicate events and route unresolved financial handoffs.

Boundary: A payment provider sees its event boundary; it cannot certify all connected systems.

Stripe — Payments / Billing · Core fintech
Payment lifecycle, integration events and recurring collection tools. Merchant setup and external banks still determine outcomes.

Product-native: Users, roles, approval queues and recorded financial actions.

Connect: Employment status, agency contracts, delegated limits and escalation contacts.

Possible help: Recommend least-privilege access and route time-sensitive approvals.

Boundary: Revoking one account does not revoke every external credential.

Stripe — Teams and roles · Core fintech
Scoped dashboard access and team administration. Outside systems and all workflow approvals are not covered.

Possible help: Show a data-access ledger and propagate permitted revocation requests.

Boundary: Service processing, sharing, retention and model training are distinct permissions.

Consent and financial-data fetch infrastructure. Requires eligible participants and permitted purpose; not unrestricted data access.

Existing capabilities and public rollout limits

Understand the Razorpay stack

These products act at different points in the merchant journey. An AI interface, a specialist agent and a payment mechanism are different product roles.

RAY / Agentic Dashboard

Ask questions about payments, settlements and refunds; retrieve reports and take supported contextual actions.

Data
Merchant payment and account records.
Merchant control
Read the underlying transaction and action before relying on it; verify current account access and supported operations.
Public status / limits
The October 2025 announcement describes early access. It is evidence of the interface direction, not universal availability.
R01 · Razorpay

RAY on WhatsApp

Payment summaries, failed-payment recovery links, settlement nudges, aggregate sales forecasts and diagnosis of payment-performance changes.

Data
Payments, settlement information and connected payment intelligence.
Merchant control
Sensitive account actions require authentication as described by Razorpay. Forecasts still need assumptions and source visibility.
Public status / limits
September 2026 announcement describes live early partners. Do not equate aggregate sales forecasting with predicting each customer’s next purchase.
R04 · Razorpay

Agent Studio

Specialists for cart recovery, failed-subscription recovery, COD confirmation, disputes and post-delivery feedback.

Data
Merchant payment records plus authorized store, order, logistics and communication sources.
Merchant control
Approved offers, scoped access, review gates, validation, consent and audit logs are described. July 2026 terms clarify that pause prevents new runs but in-progress runs may finish; authorised AI sub-processors may process data. Actual configuration and product-specific terms need confirmation.
Public status / limits
March 2026 explanation describes early access; the current product page advertises agents and sign-up. Separate marketing availability from deployment in a particular merchant account.
R02 · Razorpay, R03 · Razorpay, P01 · Razorpay

RazorpayX agentic banking

Cashflow visibility, customer-invoice follow-up and payout assistance.

Data
Connected bank balances, transactions, invoices and payout instructions.
Merchant control
Payout authorization and account permissions matter independently of the quality of the conversation.
Public status / limits
June 2026 release explicitly calls Cashflow Insights and Payout Agent beta for Connected Banking+ users; verify Receivables Agent rollout separately.
R05 · Razorpay, R06 · Razorpay

Agentic payments / commerce

Enable shopper-facing conversational discovery and payment inside supported apps or AI experiences.

Data
Merchant catalog, prices, availability and approved payment instructions.
Merchant control
Customer intent, authorization and accurate commercial terms are essential.
Public status / limits
Sprint 2026 lists announced capabilities. A launch listing alone does not show general access or identical support across channels.
R20 · Razorpay

Existing growth and payment tools

Engage/BillMe handle segmentation, offers, loyalty and campaigns; Magic Checkout handles conversion/COD; Optimizer routes payments; AutoPay supports recurring recovery.

Data
Varies by product: payment, order, customer, inventory and campaign records.
Merchant control
Merchant configuration, offer limits, workflows and product-specific permissions.
Public status / limits
Substantial overlap already exists. Public materials reviewed do not establish a complete individual reorder-prediction plus randomized incremental-profit workflow.

How to use this research

Coverage scores and their limits

Analyst-estimated coverage of the specific merchant job, not measured percent solved, product quality, market share or investment intensity.

Intensity is expressed by the same per-pain coverage score plus product focus: core fintech, fintech infrastructure, finance software or an adjacent commerce tool. A provider may be core to its own market yet score low on this particular pain.

Confidence is separate from the score. Public product documentation supports capability presence; it rarely proves merchant outcomes. Zero is a bounded research finding, not a verified absence.

Score within the specified merchant segment. Square US, Mondu UK/EU and Mercury US are design comparisons, not recommendations or proof of availability to Priya in India. No overall vendor average is presented because the scale is ordinal and the needs differ.

Native means observable by the appropriate fintech product if it is actually used—not automatically held by Razorpay. Connected data needs a permitted purpose, merchant authorization, relevant customer consent and appropriate access controls. Cross-merchant training or reuse is not assumed.

Retains all 200 original IDs and adds eight insurance/treasury pains under bucket 10. Scores and interventions are hypotheses to validate, not interview findings.

- 0 — No direct support identified in reviewed evidence; absence is unverified, not proof the company has never built it. - 1 — Enabling input or adjacent feature; the merchant still assembles most of the solution. - 2 — Partial coverage: a useful part of the job is addressed, with material gaps or limited rollout. - 3 — Substantial workflow coverage; important integrations, exceptions or manual decisions remain. - 4 — Strong documented coverage for the specified segment and configured workflow; real-world pain may remain. - 5 — Mostly addressed for a narrowly defined eligible job, supported by implementation and outcome evidence. No 5 is assigned in this desk review.

This is a desk-research map of general merchant needs, created before selecting a product opportunity. It combines official fintech and commerce product documentation with two independent research sources. Every first-person pain statement is an analyst-created hypothesis, not a quote from an interviewed merchant. Related source links establish workflow context and examples of products addressing it; they do not prove the prevalence, severity, or exact wording of each hypothesis.

The map is mutually exclusive by primary merchant job: each pain has one main home. Companies and underlying causes may span buckets. Cross-links preserve those relationships without duplicating the pain. It is collectively exhaustive only within the defined scope of general commerce and business operations. It is not an exhaustive account of every sector, jurisdiction, enterprise process, or personal circumstance. Clinical practice, detailed food safety, industrial manufacturing, regulated financial services and legal/tax obligations require their own research extensions.

The three prioritization tabs now rank all 208 pain hypotheses by primary outcome. Their weighted opportunity scores are provisional analyst judgments. The separate 0–5 provider ratings estimate documented product coverage for a specific job, not percentages solved or measured competitive performance. Frequency, severity, willingness to pay, merchant data access and current workarounds remain to be validated through interviews and observed records. A problem having a product solution does not mean the pain is solved for every merchant. A public capability not being found does not prove it is absent.

Reviewed on 13 October 2026. Most sources are vendor descriptions. Performance claims are not adopted as universal facts. The independent evidence comes from US contexts and is not extrapolated to India. US-market examples include companies founded elsewhere; the geography labels describe the relevant market, not a claim that all are US-founded startups.

Different outcomes need different measures

OutcomeMeaningBucket
New demandA suitable new customer discovers and considers the business.03
ConversionExisting interest becomes an agreed order or booking.04
Payment recoveryAn unpaid, agreed obligation becomes a verified collection.05
Delivery recoveryAn at-risk accepted order is successfully fulfilled.06
Value retentionA valid exchange or resolved dispute preserves value after costs.07
Cash recovery / releaseAlready-collected or due remittance reaches the correct bank/ledger.08
Repeat growthAn existing relationship produces additional useful purchases.09
Margin / liquidity improvementCosts or timing improve; this is not automatically new revenue.02,08,10

Validate with merchants before choosing a problem

  1. Tell me about the last sale you expected but did not complete. Show the records you used to investigate it.
  2. Walk me through yesterday from opening to closing. Where did you copy information, wait, chase someone or override a tool?
  3. Which problem repeats most often, which costs the most, and which causes the most anxiety? These can be different problems.
  4. Show one successful recovery and one failed recovery. What happened after the apparent success, including refunds and costs?
  5. Which decisions can your team make today? Which still require you, and why?
  6. What customer data is actually available and connected? Which facts do you have to ask the customer or an employee?
  7. What do you do when you are uncertain? What would make you trust a recommendation enough to approve it?
  8. When would doing nothing be better than sending another message, retrying a payment or issuing an offer?
  9. Which tool do you pay for but rarely use? Which spreadsheet or WhatsApp thread remains essential?
  10. What would you measure to decide whether an intervention was worth the money and effort?

Validate frequency, severity, workaround, data access and ability to act. The prioritization tabs identify what to validate next; they do not establish merchant demand or select a final solution.
